81:1: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement, When the sun is wrapped up. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: When the sun’s light disappears. Who said that? Al-Husayn ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Al-Fudayl ibn Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Waqid, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who narrated to me: Ubayy ibn Ka’b narrated to me: There are six signs before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun has gone. While they are like that, the stars will scatter. While they are like that, the mountains will fall to the face of the earth, and it will move, shake, and burn. The jinn will flee to the humans, and the humans will flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals will mingle and swarm among themselves. And when the wild beasts are gathered together - he said: mixed. And when the ten-year-olds are neglected - he said: their people have neglected them. And when the seas are set ablaze - he said: the jinn will say to the humans: We will bring you report. He said: So go to the seas, and behold, they will be a blazing fire. He said: While they are like that, the earth will crack with a single crack, up to the seventh lowest earth and up to the seventh highest heaven. He said: While they are like that, the wind will come to them and kill them. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, meaning: it becomes dark. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, means: it goes away. Muhammad bin Amara told me, and Ubaidullah bin Musa told me, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It fades and disappears. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: Its light is gone, so it has no light. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, regarding his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It is covered, and in Persian it is kwar takwar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement, When the sun is wrapped up, the wrapping up of the sun means its disappearance. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It is wrapped up in Persian. Others said: The meaning of this is: He threw it. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Othman bin Ali told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said, it is lowered. Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said: Muhammad bin Bishr told us, he said: Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Saleh, the same. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Badal bin Al-Muhabbir told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: I heard Ismail, he heard Abu Salih regarding his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It is thrown down. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Rabi` bin Khaitham: When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It is thrown down. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham, the same. The correct thing to say about that, according to us, is to say was rolled up as God Almighty said. Rolling up in the speech of the Arabs means gathering some things together, such as rolling up a turban, which is wrapping it around the head, and rolling up a garment, which is gathering some clothes together and wrapping them up. Likewise, His statement, When the sun is rolled up, means: gathering some of it together, then rolling it up and throwing it away. And when that was done to it, its light went away. So, according to the interpretation that we interpreted and explained for both of the statements that you mentioned from the people of interpretation, there is a correct view, and that is that if it is rolled up and thrown away, its light goes away.
81:2: And his saying: And when the stars are scattered, meaning: And when the stars are scattered from the sky and fall. The root of inkadar is pouring, as Al-Ajjaj said: I saw the vandals of Vankder's space Meaning by saying Ankadar: to be set up. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, Khaitham: And when the stars are scattered. He said: They are scattered. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, Khaitham, the same. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And when the stars are scattered, he said: they are scattered. Muhammad bin Musa bin Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi told me, he said: Muhammad bin Bishr told us, he said: Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And when the stars are scattered, he said: They are scattered. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And when the stars are scattered, he said: they fall and crumble. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when the stars are scattered, he said: They are thrown from the sky to the earth. Others said: It became disturbed: it changed. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when the stars are scattered, meaning: they change.
81:3: And His saying: And when the mountains are set in motion, meaning: And when God sets the mountains in motion, they become a mirage and scattered dust. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, And when the mountains are set in motion, he said: They go away.
81:4: His statement: And when the ten-month-old pregnant woman is neglected. “Ashar” is the plural of Ashra’, which is the woman who has completed ten months of her pregnancy. God Almighty says: And when these pregnant women, over whom their families compete, are neglected and abandoned, due to the severity of the terror that has befallen them, then how about others?! And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Husayn ibn Al-Harith told us: Al-Fudayl ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Waqid, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-A’aliyah, who said: Abi ibn Ka’b told me: And when the tithes are neglected, meaning: when their owners neglect them. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham: And when the camels are neglected, he said: Their owners are gone, they are not milked or milked. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham: And when the camels are neglected, he said: They are not milked or milked, and their owners abandon them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And when the tithes are neglected, he said: They are left alone, they are abandoned. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And when the camels are neglected, he said: The camels’ tenths. Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And when the camels are neglected, he said: Her people let her go, so she did not give milk, nor did she milk, and there was no wealth in the world more pleasing to them than her. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And when the camels are neglected, he said: The camels’ tenths are left alone. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And when the shepherds are neglected, meaning: They have no shepherd.
81:5: The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of his statement, And when the wild beasts are gathered together, so some of them said: The meaning of that is: they died. Who said that? Ali bin Muslim Al-Tusi told me: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And when the wild beasts are gathered together, he said: The gathering of the beasts means their death, and the gathering of everything means death, except for the jinn and mankind, for they will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Rabi` ibn Khaitham: And when the wild beasts are gathered together, he said: God’s command will come upon them. Sufyan said: My father said: So I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Their death will gather them together. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham, in a similar manner. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And when the beasts mix. Who said that? Al-Husayn bin Harith told us, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Musa, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-A’lia, who said: Abi bin Ka’b told me, And when the wild beasts are gathered together, he said: They will mix together. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is I gathered. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And when the wild beasts are gathered together, that these creatures will meet on the Day of Resurrection, and God will decide for them what He wills. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: The meaning of hashrat is: gathered and killed, because the well-known meaning of hashrat in the speech of the Arabs is: gathering, and from that is the saying of God, And the birds are gathered (Surah Sad: 19), meaning gathered, and His saying, So he gathered and called out (Surah al-Nazi’at 79:23). Rather, the interpretation of the Qur’an is to be carried on the most prevalent and apparent of its interpretations, not on the most unknown and unknown.
81:6: And his saying: And when the seas are set ablaze. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is when the seas are set ablaze with fire and become blazing. Who said that? Al-Husayn ibn Harith told us: Al-Fadl ibn Musa told us: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-A’aliyah, who said: Abi ibn Ka’b told me: And when the seas are set ablaze. He said: The jinn said to the humans: We will bring you report, so go to the seas, and they will be blazing with fire. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, he said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I see him as none but truthful. And the sea set ablaze (al-Tur 52:6), And when the seas are set ablaze is a lightened form. Hawthara bin Muhammad Al-Manqari told me, he said: Abu Usamah told us, he said: Mujalid told us, he said: An old man from Bajila told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: God wraps the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sea, then sends upon them a violent wind, which blows it until it becomes fire. That is what He said, And when the seas are set ablaze. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: They will be set ablaze on the Day of Resurrection. They claimed that this setting ablaze is in the speech of the Arabs. Ibn Hamid told us: Ya`qub told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar ibn `Atiyyah, regarding His statement, And the sea set ablaze (al-Tur 52:6), he said: It is like the set ablaze And when the seas are set ablaze like it. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: lit. Others said: The meaning of this is: it overflowed. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Rabi` bin Khaitham: And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: they overflow. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Rabi’, similarly. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Kalbi, regarding his statement, And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: Filled. Do you not see that he said, And the sea set ablaze (al-Tur 52:6). It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And when the seas are set ablaze, meaning: they burst forth. Others said: Rather, he meant that its water was gone. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: Its water is gone and not a drop remains in it. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And when the seas are set ablaze. He said: Its water will sink and disappear. Al-Husayn bin Muhammad Al-Dhara’ told me: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Husayn, regarding this word And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: They dry up. Al-Husayn bin Muhammad told us: Yazid bin Zari’ told us: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: They dry up. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: it was filled until it overflowed, then it burst forth and flowed as God described it in another place, when He said: And when the seas burst forth. The Arabs say of a river or a filled pool: flowing water. From this is the saying of Labid: They were in the middle of the secret show and a crack, closed and adjacent to her pen Filled with water. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as sajart with a shaddah on the j. Some Basra readers read it with a light jim. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
81:7: And his saying: And when souls are paired, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: He attached each person to his form, and he was placed between the types and the examples. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of An-Nu`man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him: And when souls are paired, he said: They are two men who do one deed and by it they enter Paradise and by it they enter Hell. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: And when souls are paired, he said: They are two men who do a deed and enter Paradise because of it. And he said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses (al-Saffat 37:22), he said: Their peers. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: And when souls are paired, he said: They are two men who do a deed, and because of it they will enter Paradise or Hell. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, that he heard An-Nu`man bin Bashir say: I heard `Umar bin Al-Khattab while he was delivering a sermon, and he said: “And you were three groups. The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? And the foremost - the foremost. Those are the ones brought near.” (Al-Waqi`ah: 7-8-9-10-11) Then he said: And when souls are paired. He said: Pairs in Paradise and pairs in Hell. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was asked about the statement of God, And when souls are paired, he said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man will be paired with an evil man in Hell. Muhammad bin Khalaf told me: Muhammad bin Al-Sabah Al-Dulabi told us, on the authority of Al-Walid, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Umar, who said: And when souls are paired, he said: The pairs are each man with each people who used to do his work, and that is because God says: “And you will be three groups. * So the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? * And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? * And the foremost - the foremost.” (al-Waqi’ah 56:7-8-9-10) He said: They are the pairs. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when souls are paired, he said: That is when people will be in three pairs. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And when souls are paired, he said: Every person will be joined to his followers. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And when souls are paired, he said: People of equal status are brought together. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And when souls are paired, he said: Every person will join his own group, the Jews with the Jews, and the Christians with the Christians. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Khaitham: And when souls are paired, he said: He will be gathered with the one who did his work. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, who said: A man comes with his employer. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that is that the souls were returned to the bodies and paired with them: that is, they were given a mate. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, And when the souls are paired, he said: The souls return to the bodies. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that he said regarding this verse, And when the souls are paired, he said: The bodies are paired, so the souls are returned to the bodies. Ubaid bin Asbat bin Muhammad told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah: And when the souls are paired, he said: The spirits are paired with the bodies. Al-Hasan bin Zuraiq Al-Tahri told me: Asbat told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement, And when the souls are paired, he said: The souls are paired with the bodies. The first of the two interpretations of this is the correct one, which was interpreted by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, for the reason he cited, which is the statement of God Almighty: And you were three groups (al-Waqi’ah 56:7), and His statement: Gather together those who did wrong and their partners (al-Saffat 37:22). These are undoubtedly examples and examples, in good and evil, and likewise His statement: And when souls are paired with peers and examples in good and evil. Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Abd Al-Aziz bin Muslim Al-Qasmali told us on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, regarding his statement, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: Its beginning will come while the people are watching, and its end will come when the souls are paired.
81:8: And his saying: And when the girl buried alive is asked * For what sin was she killed? The reciters differed in the reading of that. Abu al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih read it And when the girl buried alive is asked * For what sin was she killed meaning: The girl buried alive asks the buryers: For what sin did they kill her. The narration mentioned that: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, regarding his statement And when the girl buried alive is asked, he said: She is asked for her blood. Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Abu Al-Dhaha said: And when the girl buried alive asks He said: I asked her killer. If a reader who read I asked had read For what sin were you killed? it would have had a point, and the meaning of that would have been for the one who read For what sin were you killed? However, if it was a narration, both meanings would be permissible, as it is said: Abdullah said, For what sin was he struck? as Antarah said: The one who insults me is my honor, and I did not insult them, and the one who vows that if I meet them, my blood will be shed This is because they used to say: If we meet his family, we will kill him. So Antarah narrated their words in his poetry, and likewise the other’s words: Two men from Dhuba told us that they saw a naked man. Meaning: They told us that, but the speech was based on the narrative method, and some of the common reciters of the regions read it as: And when the girl buried alive is asked * For what sin was she killed? meaning the girl buried alive, for what sin was she killed, and the meaning of killed is killed, except that it was returned to the report of the form of a narrative in the manner of the past statement before, and the meaning of that may be directed to be: And when the girl buried alive is asked, her killers and those who buried her alive, For what sin did they kill her? Then it was returned to what did not name the perpetrator, so it was said: For what sin was she killed. The first of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the correct reading: the reading of the one who reads it I was asked with a damma on the seen for what sin were you killed in the form of a report, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, and the buried alive is: the one buried alive, and this is what the Arabs used to do with their daughters, and from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq bin Ghalib: And among us is he who revived the lost, and the absent and Amr, and among us are those who carry and defend. It is said: He buried him alive, so he buried him alive, burying him alive. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And when the girl buried alive is asked: In some readings it is: She is asked for what sin she was killed, not for what sin. The people of the Age of Ignorance would kill their daughter and feed her dog, so God condemned them for that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: “Qais ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I buried eight daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era.’ He said: ‘Then free a camel for each one.’” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya’la, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham: And when the girl buried alive is asked, he said: The Arabs were among the people who did this. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Rabi` bin Khaitham, with a similar chain of transmission. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when the girl buried alive is asked, he said: The girls whom the Arab groups used to kill, and he read, For what sin were you killed?
81:9: God Almighty said: For what sin were you killed?
81:10: And His statement: And when the records are spread out, God Almighty says: And when the records of the servants’ deeds are spread out for them, after they were folded up with what was written in them of good and bad deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when the pages are spread out, is your page, O son of Adam. You fill out what is in it, then it is folded, then it is spread out for you on the Day of Resurrection. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as nashr with a light shin, and some of the Kufians also read it likewise. Some of the reciters of Mecca and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a heavy shin. Those who were ill-advised among them recited it likewise, based on the statement of God, that he will be given spread-out pages (Al-Muddathir: 52). He did not say manshurah, but rather the emphasis was appropriate in it, because it is a report about a group, as one says, These are slaughtered rams. If he had reported about one person with that, it would have been lightened, and it would have been said madbuha, and so is his statement manshurah.
81:11: God Almighty says: And when the sky is taken away and drawn away, then folded up. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Kashtat, he said: I pulled. And it was mentioned that that is in the reading of Abdullah: Qashtat with a qaf. And qasht and katsht have the same meaning, and that is a conversion by the Arabs of the kaf to a qaf, because of the similarity of their points of articulation, just as camphor is called qafur, and qast is called kasat, and that is common in their speech, if the points of articulation of two letters are similar, they substitute each other for each, like their saying for the fire-places athathi, and a garment raqbi and thraqbi.
81:12: And His statement: And when Hell is set ablaze, God Almighty says: And when Hell is set ablaze and is heated. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And when Hell is set ablaze. Its blaze is the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as sa’arat with a shaddah on the ‘ayn, meaning he lit it again and again. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it without a shaddah. The statement about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.
81:13: And His saying: And when Paradise is brought near, God Almighty says: And when Paradise is brought near and brought near. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of Ar-Rabi` ibn Khaitham: And when Hell is set ablaze, and when Paradise is brought near. He said: The hadith goes to these two: A group in Paradise, and a group in the Blaze. Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ya`la, on the authority of al-Rabi`, And when Hell is set ablaze * And when Paradise is brought near. He said: The hadith has gone to these two: a group in Paradise, and a group in Hell. Al-Rabi` meant by his saying: The hadith has gone to these two: that the beginning of the report When the sun is wrapped up… to His saying And when Hell is set ablaze only refers to the events that will come to an end, one of these two things, and that destination is either Paradise or Hell.
81:14: And His statement: A soul will know what it has brought, God Almighty says: At that time, a soul will know what it has brought of good, which will lead it to Paradise, or evil, which will lead it to Hell. He says: At that time, it will become clear to him what he was ignorant of, and what was good for him in it, unlike anything else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, A soul will know what it has brought of deeds. He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: The hadith goes on to this. His saying, A soul will know what it has brought is an answer to his saying, When the sun is wrapped up and what follows it, just as it is said, When Abdullah stands, Amr sits.
81:15: And His statement: So I swear by the stars that recede, * that move swiftly and sweep away. The people of interpretation differed regarding the stars that recede, that move swiftly and sweep away. Some of them said: They are the five bright stars that recede in their courses and then return, and sweep away and hide in their homes, as gazelles sweep away in their caves. The five stars are: Bahram, Saturn, Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter. Who said that? Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, that a man stood up to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: What is the sweeping stars? He said: They are the stars. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, he said: I heard Khalid bin Arara, peace be upon him, when he was asked about I swear by the stars that recede, the stars that move, the stars that sweep away, he said: They are the stars that recede during the day and sweep away at night. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The stars. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Murad, on the authority of Ali, that he said: Do you know what Al-Khuns is? They are the stars that move at night and set during the day. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Jarir ibn Hazim told me, that he heard Al-Hasan being asked, and it was said: O Abu Saeed, what are the sweeping maidens? He said: The stars. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Hudha bin Khalifa told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah, regarding his statement, So I swear by the stars that recede, * That move about and sweep away, he said: They are the shining stars that move towards the east. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They are the stars. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Murad, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: So I swear by the stars that recede, * that move about and sweep away. He said: He means the stars, which sweep away during the day and appear at night. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So I swear by the stars that recede, * that move about and sweep away, he said: They are the stars that appear at night and disappear during the day. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His statement, So I swear by the stars that recede, * that move and sweep away, he said: They are the stars that recede during the day, and the stars that move and sweep away are their movements when they disappear. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, The stars that withdraw, the swift ones, the sweeping ones. He said: The stars that withdraw, and the swift ones, the sweeping ones, are the stars that withdraw, they withdraw from their rising, they are delayed every year for them, every year there is a delay in hastening that rising, they withdraw from it, and the sweeping ones: they are swept away during the day and are not seen. He said: And the swift ones run after, so this is the sweeping ones, the swift ones, the sweeping ones. Others said: It is the wild cows that sweep in their lair. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Hisham bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Zakariya bin Abi Zaida, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, that he said to Abu Maysarah: What are the sweeping slave girls? He said: They are wild cows. He said: I also see that. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement, the wild cows. He said: wild cows. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Shurahbil, who said: Ibn Masoud said: O Amr, are the slave girls the sweeping creatures, or do you not see them? Amr said: I see them as cows. Abdullah said: I see them as cows too. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said: I asked Abdullah about it, and he mentioned something similar. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Jarir ibn Hazim told me, he said: Al-Ajaj ibn al-Mundhir told me, he said: I asked Abu al-Sha’tha’ Jabir ibn Zayd about the sweeping slave girls, he said: They are the cows when they sweep their nests. Yunus said, Abdullah bin Wahb told me: It is the cows when they flee from the wolves, and that is what he meant by his saying, They swept their nests. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Jarir said, and Al-Salt bin Rashid told me, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, the wild cows. He said: They are wild cows. Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said: Mujahid was asked while we were with Ibrahim about his statement, The burrows are the ones that hide. He said, I do not know. Ibrahim rebuked him and said, Why do you not know? He said, They narrate on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and we used to hear that it means cows. Ibrahim said, “They are cows. The burrows are the ones that hide, and the burrows are the ones that hide.” Yaqub narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid, that they discussed this verse: So I swear by the stars that recede, * The stars that move about, and they sweep away. Ibrahim said to Mujahid: Say what you heard about it. Mujahid said: We used to hear something about it, and people said: They are the stars. Ibrahim said: They are lying about Ali, may God be pleased with him. This is as they narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he included the lower in the higher, and the higher in the lower. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, who said: Mujahid was asked about the sweeping maidens. He said: I do not know. They claim that they are cows. Ibrahim said: What? You do not know that they are cows. He said: They say on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that they are the stars. He said: They lie about Ali, peace be upon him. Others said: It is the gazelle. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, So I swear by the receding, the swiftly gliding gazelles, meaning the gazelles. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: So I swear by the stars that recede. He said: The gazelles. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So I swear by the stars that recede, * That move swiftly and sweep away, he said: We used to say, I think he said: the gazelles, until Saeed bin Jubayr claimed that he asked Ibn Abbas about them, so he repeated the recitation to him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The gazelles that hide, the swift ones that run after them, meaning the gazelles. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty swore by things that sometimes disappear, that is, they disappear, and sometimes they flow and are swept away, and their sweeping away means that they take refuge in their places, and the places where wild cows and gazelles take refuge, and the singular is mukanis and kanās, as al-A’sha said: When we reached the neighborhood, Anas was covered in dirt as a hyena is covered in dirt under a broom. This is the plural of Muknaz, as Tarafa bin Al-Abd said about Al-Kanaz: As if the lost sweepers were covering it and the frames of the cross under the cross of the supporter As for the evidence that the sweeper may be for gazelles, it is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: Have you not seen that God sent down rain and the gazelles dusted themselves in the dugouts? The word kanas in Arabic speech is what I have described, and it is not strange that it is used as a metaphor for the places where the stars are in the sky. If that is the case, and there is no indication in the verse that what is meant by that is the stars and not the cows, nor the cows and not the gazelles, then it is correct to include by that everything whose characteristic is sometimes snoring and other times running, and the sweeping with groans is as God Almighty has described its characteristic.
81:16: God Almighty said: The neighborhood is the sweeping.
81:17: Our Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, swears by the night when it covers with darkness. He says: And I swear by the night when it covers with darkness. The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement, And the night when it covers with darkness. Some of them said: What he meant by his statement, when it covers with darkness, is when it departs. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the night when it covers means: when it departs. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the night when it covers means: when it departs. Abdul Hami bin Bayan Al-Yashkari told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Dhabian, who said: I was following Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, as he was going out towards the east. He faced the dawn and recited this verse: And the night when it covers. Abu Kurayb narrated: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ubaidullah, on the authority of Saad bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman, who said: Ali, peace be upon him, came out from the door of the market, and the dawn had risen. He recited: By the night when it covers with darkness, and by the morning when it breathes. Where is the one who asked about the Witr prayer? Yes, this is the time for Witr. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the night when it covers: he said: its approach, and it is said: its departure. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the night when it covers means when it departs. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: When it darkens means: when it turns away. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement, When it darkens: when it turns away. Abu Kurayb narrated: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, came out after the muezzin had called the dawn prayer and said: By the night when it covers its darkness * And by the morning when it breathes. Where is the one who asked about the witr prayer? He said: Yes, this is the time for the witr prayer. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the night when it covers with darkness, he said: Covers with darkness: turns away, and he said: The dawn breathed from here, and he pointed to the east, the rising of dawn. Others said: What he meant by his saying when it darkens is when it approaches with its darkness. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan: And the night when it covers the people. He said: When it covers the people. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Fudayl, on the authority of Atiyah: And the night when it covers He said: He pointed with his hand to the west. The more correct of the two interpretations in my opinion is the one that says: The meaning of that is: when it has passed, and that is his statement: And the morning when it breathes, which indicates that the oath is by the night when it has passed, and by the day when it is approaching. The Arabs say: The night has darkened and The night has darkened when it has passed and nothing remains of it except a little. Among the sayings about that is the statement of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: Oh Hind, how quickly you can run, even if only a man could follow the breeze. This is the language of those who say: Sa’sa’. As for the language of those who say: As’as, it is the saying of Alqamah ibn Qart: Until the morning breathes its breath and the night departs from it and darkens It means to turn away. Some people who know the Arabic language claim that ‘asas means to approach from the beginning and become dark. Al-Farra’ said: Abu al-Bilad the grammarian used to recite a verse: He can even, if He wills, draw near to us a light from Him. He says: If He willed, when He drew near, but He assimilated the dhal into the dal. Al-Farra’ said: So they thought that this verse was fabricated.
81:18: And his saying: And the morning when it breathes means: The light of day when it comes and becomes clear. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, And the morning when it breathes, he said: When it arises. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the morning when it breathes: when it shines and approaches.
81:19: And His statement: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger, God Almighty says: Indeed, this Qur’an is the revelation of a noble Messenger, meaning Gabriel, who revealed it to Muhammad ibn Abdullah. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, that he used to say: It is the word of a noble Messenger, meaning: Gabriel. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that he used to say, It is the word of a noble Messenger. He said, It is Gabriel.
81:20: And His statement: Possessor of power, secure in the presence of the Lord of the Throne. God Almighty says: Possessor of power, meaning Gabriel, over whatever task he is charged with, not helpless in the presence of the Lord of the Throne. Secure, meaning: He is secure in the presence of the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
81:21: God Almighty says: Obeyed then meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him, obeyed in heaven, the angels obey him. Trustworthy meaning: Trustworthy with God in His revelation and His message, and other things that He entrusted him with. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Omar bin Shabib Al-Masli told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh: Obeyed and then trustworthy. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, is trustworthy, but he will not enter seventy canopies of light without permission. Muhammad bin Mansur al-Tusi told us: Omar bin Shabib told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us: I do not know it except on the authority of Abu Salih, similarly. Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Aqta’ told us: My father, Umar ibn Khalid, told me, on the authority of Muqal ibn Ubayd God al-Jazari, who said: Maymun ibn Mihran said regarding His statement, Obeyed and then trustworthy, that he was Gabriel, peace be upon him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Possessor of power with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established, obeyed and trustworthy, he said: He means Gabriel. Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Of power with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established, obeyed “Obeyed with God” then trustworthy. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Obeyed and then trustworthy, meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him.
81:22: And His statement: And your companion is not mad. God Almighty says: And your companion, O people, Muhammad is not mad, speaking of a madman, and raving like madmen. Rather, he came with the truth and confirmed the messengers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Barqi told us, he said: My father Umar ibn Khalid told us, on the authority of Muqal ibn Ubayd God al-Jazari, he said: Maymun ibn Mihran said: And your companion is not mad. He said: That is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
81:23: And His statement: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon, God Almighty says: And Muhammad, Gabriel, peace be upon him, saw him in his form on the side that makes things clear, so they are seen from before them, and that is from the direction of the rising of the sun from the east. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, on the clear horizon, the highest, he said: on a horizon from around Ajyad. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, By the clear horizon. He said: We were told that the horizon is where the sun rises. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And he saw him on the clear horizon, we used to say that it is the horizon from which the day comes. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon, he said: He saw Gabriel on the clear horizon. Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Al-Aizar, who said: I heard Abu Al-Ahwas say about the words of God, And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon, that he saw Gabriel with six hundred wings in his form. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Amir, who said: Gabriel only saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his original form once. He used to come to him in the form of a man called Dihya. When he saw him in his original form, he had covered the entire horizon, wearing green brocade with pearls hanging from it. This is what God said: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon. He mentioned that this verse: When the sun is wrapped up “Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger” is about Gabriel, up to His saying: And he is not stingy with the unseen, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And his saying: And He is not stingy with the unseen. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it as bidhanin with a dhad, meaning: He is not stingy with them in teaching them what God taught him and revealed to him from His Book. Some of the Meccans, some of the Basrans, some of the commentators, and some of the Kufians recited it as bidhanin with a dhad, meaning that he is not accused of what he tells them about God from the prophets. Mention of those who said that with the letter Ḍād, and its interpretation is as we described from the interpretation of the people of interpretation. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur: (And he is not a suspect of the unseen) He said: The suspect is the accused, and in your reading it is stingy and the stingy is the miser, and the unseen is the Qur’an. Bishr told us, he said: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Wasiti told us, he said: Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim: And he is not stingy with the unseen. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And He is not stingy with regard to the unseen, he said: He does not stingy with you regarding what He knows. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And he is not stingy with regard to the unseen, he said: This Qur’an is hidden, so God gave it to Muhammad, so he gave it away, taught it, and called people to it. By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not stingy with it. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur and he is not suspicious of the unseen he said: In our reading it is mththumum, and whoever reads it bdhnin says: bbghil. Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, He is not stingy with the unseen. He said: He is miserly. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He is not stingy with regard to the unseen, the unseen is the Qur’an. He did not withhold it from any of the people. He conveyed it and communicated it. God sent with it the trustworthy spirit, Gabriel, to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Gabriel conveyed what God entrusted to Muhammad, and Muhammad conveyed what God and Gabriel entrusted to the servants. None of them was stingy, nor concealed, nor did they lie. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aamer: And he is not stingy with the unseen, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mention of those who said that with the letter Dhad, and interpreted it according to what we mentioned from the people of interpretation. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he read with suspicion, he said: He is not accused. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Mu`alla, on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Jubayr: He used to recite this verse And he is not a suspect of the unseen. So I said to Sa`id Ibn Jubayr: What is the suspect? He said: He is not accused. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mu’alla, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, that he recited: And he is not a suspect of the unseen. I said: And who is the suspect? He said: The accused. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement and he is not a suspect of the unseen means: He is not accused of what he brought, and he is not suspected of what he was given. Bishr told us, he said: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Wasiti told us, he said: Al-Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim And the unseen is not something to be suspected of, he said: It is something to be accused of. Abu Kuraib told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur and he is not a suspect of the unseen he said: The unseen is the Qur’an... and in our reading a suspect is accused. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement with suspicion: He said: There is no one who is accused of what God has revealed. Some Arab scholars have interpreted this to mean: He is not weak in knowing the unseen, but he is able to bear it and bear it. This is based on the Arabs’ saying about a weak man: He is suspicious. The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct one: what the scripts of the Muslims’ Qur’ans agree upon, even if their readings of it differ, and that is badhanin with the letter ḍād, because all of that is like that in their scripts. If that is the case, then the more correct interpretation is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it: And Muhammad, despite what God taught him of His revelation and sending down, is not stingy with teaching it to you, O people. Rather, he is eager for you to believe in it and learn it.
81:25: And His statement: And it is not the word of an accursed devil. God Almighty says: This Qur’an is not the word of an accursed, banished devil, but it is the word of God and His revelation.
81:26: And His saying: So where do you go? God Almighty says: So where do you go from this Qur’an, and turn away from it? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, So where are you going? He says: So where do you deviate from My Book and My obedience? And it was said: So where are you going? He did not say: So where are you going, as it is said: The Levant is gone, and the market is gone. And it was narrated from the Arabs by hearing: The valley took him away, in the sense of canceling the description. And some of the Banu Uqayl may have recited: Hanifa shouted at us when she saw us, and which land goes to shout Meaning: To which land are you going? It is permissible to omit the adjective in this case due to usage.
81:27: God Almighty says: This Qur’an, and His saying: It from the mention of the Qur’an is only a reminder to the worlds He says: is only a reminder and an admonition to the worlds of jinn and mankind.
81:28: God Almighty said: For whoever among you wills to go straight. So He, the Most High, made that a reminder for whoever among the worlds wills to go straight, and He did not make it for all of them. So the lam in His saying For whoever among you wills is a replacement for the lam in for the worlds. The meaning of the statement was: It is only a reminder for whoever among you wills to go straight on the path of truth, so he follows it and believes in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, For whoever among you wills to go straight, he said: Follows the truth.
81:29: And His saying: And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills. God Almighty says: And you do not will, O people, to be steadfast upon the truth, except that God wills that for you. He mentioned that the reason for which this verse was revealed is: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa, when the verse, For whoever among you wills to go straight, was revealed, Abu Jahl said: That is up to us. If we will, we will go straight. Then the verse, And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills, was revealed. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: When this verse was revealed, For whoever among you wills to go straight, Abu Jahl said: The matter is up to us. If we want to go straight, we will go straight, and if we want to, we will not go straight. Then God revealed, And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills. Ibn Al-Barqi told me: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa, who said: When this verse was revealed, For whoever among you wills to go straight, Abu Jahl said: That is up to us. If we want to go straight, we will go straight, and if we want to, we will not go straight. Then God revealed, And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills.
